task: phase B plan 3, task 5 -- the offline lightmap baker
outcome: The pack ships on serenity only. Linear-domain contrast (tools/luminance.py, the quantity task 6 gates on) moved 3.384 -> 3.385 against a criterion of >= 4.9 and photographs at 6.196: the offline bake is flat on that measure. Mean luminance moved toward the photographs (0.2819 -> 0.2891 against 0.2993) and p5 moved away from them (0.0833 -> 0.0854 against 0.0483), which is what a bounce term does -- it fills the near-field shadows the runtime bake crushes to black. All-spot legacy dE2000 moved 16.59 -> 16.75, away from the 16.58 gate. Task 6 owns the verdict.
method: Every spawns[] entry rendered at 480x300 through the full post chain at pixelRatio 1, pixels pooled across all spawns before the mean and the INTERPOLATED 5th percentile of Rec.709 luma on the sRGB-encoded frame (0-255). Same method and same harness as <apt>-b3-task2-luminance.json and <apt>-b3-task3-luminance.json. NOT comparable to tools/luminance.py, which reports linear-light values over a different population.
harness: Playwright headless Chromium with --use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist. The default headless GPU is SwiftShader, which post.js's capable() rejects -- a run without these flags silently measures with no post chain. Spawn yaw is asserted against the raw JSON degrees on every run. Each phase is a separate page load; the run-to-run spread measured on an identical build is 0.1 of meanL and 0.0 of p5L (BASE-fef2d07 measured twice: 138.7/80.0 and 138.6/80.0).

roundTrip.note: every surface decoded back from the WebP it ships as and compared with the canvas it came from; Chrome toDataURL(image/webp, 1) is lossless here

runtime-bake.note: The runtime bake, this branch, with tour/lightmaps/serenity/ moved aside so Lightmaps.load() reports "missing" and every surface falls through to bakeSurface(). The before column.
issues: lightmaps: no readable manifest at lightmaps/serenity/ (HTTP 404)

offline-pack.note: The committed offline pack loaded instead: 10 of 10 surfaces, window.__lightmaps.status "ok".

offline-pack-bounces0.note: PIPELINE IDENTITY CHECK, never committed: the same pack re-baked with bounces = 0, at which the integrator reduces exactly to bake.js own AMB_RGB x escaped-fraction estimator. It reproduces the runtime bake to the reported precision, which is what proves the texel mapping, the WebP encoding, the loading, the colour space and the lightMapIntensity are all neutral -- so the shipped pack row differs by the integrator and nothing else.

withdrawn-3x-bounces0.note: WITHDRAWN, not shipped: 3x texel density, bounces = 0. Recorded because it is the evidence for why resScale stayed at 1 -- at 3x the texels are finer than the 0.14 m wall is thick, bake.js edge dilation replaces exactly one ring and takes its replacement from a neighbour that is itself spoiled, and the ceilings come back with a hard black band (13/255 against an interior of 185).

withdrawn-3x-bounces2-128rays.note: WITHDRAWN, not shipped: 3x texel density, 2 bounces, at the 128-ray pipeline-validation bake rather than the shipped 2048. Carries the same black-band artefact as the row above, so its apparent contrast gain (1.757) is partly the artefact and must not be read as the offline bake working. The 2048-ray 3x run measured the same 139.7 / 79.5 / 1.757 but its harness file was overwritten by the re-run at resScale 1, so this file is the one that survives.

BASE-fef2d07.note: The branch tip this task started from, served from a separate git worktree on port 8743. Present to show that the bake.js and sampler.js refactors are behaviour-neutral when no pack is loaded, not to be compared with the pack.

linearLuminance.note: Linear-light Rec.709 relative luminance over the compare spots, captured at ?fov=legacy. Diagnostic only -- no gate is taken from it here. Contrast is mean/p5, quoted so the render can be compared with the photographs. This is the number task 6 applies its >= 4.9 criterion to.

bakeMs.note: window.__bakeMs, five fresh page loads per side, twice. With a pack it covers the manifest fetch, the SHA-256, the ten texture loads and the wall/furniture passes, which still run unchanged. THE TWO PAIRED RUNS DISAGREE IN SIGN -- the no-pack side alone moved from a median of 1237 ms to 2680 ms between them on identical code -- so no net load-time claim is supportable from them. The usable measurement is packCost below, taken inside single page loads: the texel loop a pack skips costs 215-294 ms for all ten surfaces, and the eleven /lightmaps/ requests cost 4.5-6.8 s of wall time against tools/serve.py. The pack does not buy load time.

phases.note: window.__bakeMs, five fresh page loads per side; see the report -- the two paired runs disagree in sign and no net claim is supportable from them. The decomposition in packCost is the usable measurement.

packCost.note: measured inside one page load each, three loads: texelLoopMs is Baker.bakeSurface re-run at runtime settings over all 10 surfaces (exactly what a pack skips); packFetchMs is the wall time of the 11 /lightmaps/ requests against tools/serve.py
